prompt:
Write a three.js ES module: export function buildCampus(THREE, opts, kit) -> THREE.Group, the ground and scenery of a miniature campus map for a downtown New York university neighbourhood, 64 wide (x from -32 to 32) by 40 deep (z from -20 to 20). Four special buildings will be placed by the host on four empty paved plots, so leave them clear: each plot is 9 by 8, centred at (-20, 0, -8), (20, 0, -8), (-20, 0, 9), (20, 0, 9), drawn as pale stone paving with a darker edge, each with a path to the centre. In the centre a city park square about 20 by 16: lawns, radiating stone paths, a white marble triumphal arch about 5 high on the north side, a round fountain with a basin, a central jet and translucent water, benches, lamp posts, and autumn trees in orange, gold and red. Around the square a street grid: asphalt streets with lane dashes and crosswalks, sidewalks, a bus with a shelter, a few yellow taxis. Along the outer edges, rows of scenery buildings in softer, slightly desaturated colours so the four special buildings stand out: brownstone rows with stoops, brick academic halls, one tall red sandstone block, one glass building, with roof details and inset windows, each 3 to 9 high. Violet banners on lamp posts. Trees as rounded canopies on trunks (InstancedMesh). Also export const PLOTS = { library: [-20, 0, -8], clubs: [20, 0, -8], commons: [-20, 0, 9], career: [20, 0, 9] }, export const HOME = [0, 0, 14] (where the player's character stands when it arrives), and export const WALKWAYS: for each plot name an array of [x, z] points forming a path from HOME to just in front of that plot along the paths. opts = { accent } (banner colour, default violet).

STYLE (the same as the dorm-room diorama the player already knows): a refined, cozy, stylised 3D miniature like a premium life-sim game. Smooth, rounded forms (bevelled boxes, lathe shapes, extruded bezier shapes with bevels; no raw sharp boxes), believable architecture, small secondary details, warm colours. MeshStandardMaterial with thoughtful roughness; castShadow and receiveShadow on meshes. Windows are inset panes with frames; lit windows use a warm emissive colour. Paint brick, stone, roof tiles, wood and paving as textures in code with kit.canvasTexture(width, height, (ctx, w, h) => {...}) (it returns a THREE.CanvasTexture; set wrap and repeat yourself). No text, no letters, no logos.

RULES: a plain ES module; no imports; no globals: THREE and kit arrive as arguments and are passed on to helpers. No document, window, fetch or storage. Units: 1 unit = about 3 metres of campus, Y up. Keep the triangle count moderate (under about 40,000) by reusing geometries and materials and by using InstancedMesh for repeated things such as windows, trees and lamp posts. Keep the module under 1,200 lines. Return only the code in one ```js block.
